assumptions: FIX (f32 path): all four matmul sites of `_solve_head` now go through `jax.lax.dot(..., precision=lax.DotAlgorithmPreset.F32_F32_F32)`. The four sites are: (1) the seed `power = N @ N`; (2) inside the Neumann loop `t_mat = t_mat @ (power + eye)`; (3) inside the same loop `power = power @ power`; (4) the final `t_mat @ bv`. For C=64 the loop runs _inverse_steps(64)=5 times, so the body traces 11 `dot_general` nodes (the last `power @ power` is dead after the loop and DCE'd); all 11 carry the pinned precision. There is no other multiplication or reduction in the body — `jnp.eye`, `jnp.tril`, the adds, the loads/stores are elementwise/select.

WHY THAT PRESET: `DotAlgorithmPreset.F32_F32_F32` is the explicit IEEE branch of the Pallas-Triton lowerer `jax/_src/pallas/triton/lowering.py::_dot_general_lowering` — it becomes `tt.dot(input_precision=IEEE)`, i.e. exactly the task's `input_precision="ieee"`, spelled through the api the body actually uses. It was preferred over `Precision.HIGHEST` because it states the whole algorithm (f32 in, f32 accumulator, f32 out) rather than relying on the lowerer's `_TF32_PRECISIONS` tuple membership.

ROOT CAUSE (reproduced on the host): `check_kernel.py` runs on the GB10 *without* `net/tests/conftest.py`, so the ambient `jax_default_matmul_precision` is unset there. A bare `a @ b` then traces `dot_general` with `precision=None`, which the same lowerer maps to `(Precision.DEFAULT, Precision.DEFAULT)` and Triton resolves to **tf32** for f32 operands. Measured on this host: with the ambient policy unset the pre-fix body traced `precision=None` on every dot; under conftest's `highest` the same dots became `(HIGHEST, HIGHEST)` (IEEE) — which is precisely why the CPU suite was green while the GB10 verdict was tf32 (max_abs ~3.6e-3, 61% of entries outside 1e-4).

PRECISION SOURCE: the pin is chosen from the *declared case dtype* inside `_build_kernel`'s body closure (and identically in `solve_jax`), via the new `_matmul_precision(dtype)` helper — not from the ambient policy. f32 -> the IEEE preset; bf16 -> `None`. Because both the Pallas body and the host path use the same helper, the two paths run the same arithmetic and the CPU parity verdict remains a verdict on the kernel's program.

bf16 LEFT AS IS (per task item 1): bf16 keeps `precision=None`, i.e. the backend default (tf32 on tensor cores). It already passes with 0% of entries outside the (2e-2, 2e-2) pair, its verdict is dominated by the bf16 input/output rounding, and the fix is scoped to the f32 arithmetic. Verified: the bf16 body still tracks the ambient policy (None -> None, `highest` -> (HIGHEST, HIGHEST)).

NO CONFLICT WITH ADR-010: ADR-010 pins `jax_default_matmul_precision` in `net/tests/conftest.py` as the single place for the *suite's* verdict. This change pins the precision inside the *kernel artifact* so it holds on its own under `check_kernel.py` (which has no conftest). Both serve ADR-010's principle ('the verdict must not depend on the environment'); they act at different layers, so `conflicts_with_prior_decisions` is empty.

TOLERANCE UNCHANGED: `TOLERANCE['float32'] = (1e-4, 1e-4)` is left exactly as the contract declares it (SPEC: 'порог 1e-4 не меняется'). The alternative of keeping tf32 and loosening the tolerance was explicitly NOT taken — that is an architect's decision, not a silent test weakening.

PUBLIC CONTRACT UNCHANGED: no change to `CASES`, `TOLERANCE`, `TUNE_SPACE`, `DEFAULT_PARAMS`, `make_inputs`, `kernel`, `reference`, `baseline`, `cost`, `valid_config`, nor to `block_shape`/`grid` (`_block_specs`), `net/kda.py` or `net/config.json`. Only the private `_solve_head` gained a `precision` argument (plus the new private `_matmul_precision` helper).

TESTS (host, `net/tests/test_kernel_kda_ut_solve.py`): 20 passed = the 17 pre-existing tests plus 3 new ones in section 4. The f32 parity against `jnp.linalg.solve` still holds inside the previous atol=1e-4 (measured max_abs < 1e-5), and the Pallas-interpreter layout test still executes the same body with the preset.

NEW REGRESSION GUARD: section 4 of the test file reads the traced `pallas_call` body jaxpr and asserts (a) every `dot_general` carries `F32_F32_F32` for f32, (b) the dot count equals the product form's unroll (2*_inverse_steps(C)+1/+2), and (c) the pin survives a hostile ambient policy (`jax.default_matmul_precision('default')`/`'high'`) while bf16 keeps tracking the policy. Sensitivity verified: setting the module constant to None makes the guard fail.

open_questions: PERFORMANCE (measured by the architect on the GB10): the IEEE f32 dot path may be slower than tf32 on tensor cores — tf32 is Triton's default for f32 precisely because it is faster. No GPU run was allowed here, so the cost of this change was not measured; `bench.py` on the GB10 should report it. This is the conscious trade-off the task calls for: accuracy over speed.

ALTERNATIVE NOT TAKEN (architect's call): keep tf32 and either loosen the f32 tolerance or pin `jax_default_matmul_precision` in the `check_kernel.py` harness. Both change a declared threshold/contract, so they were left to the architect rather than applied silently.

OBSERVABILITY GAP: the suite's own policy (conftest pins `highest`) makes a `precision=None` body still trace an IEEE-equivalent `(HIGHEST, HIGHEST)` on the host, so this bug class is invisible to the CPU suite and only surfaced on the GB10. The new guard closes that gap by asserting the exact preset, not merely 'some IEEE value'.
